bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: West Asia conflict impacting energy/LNG supplies; Chinese PVC dumping undermining domestic prices; Ethanol policy bottlenecks (low OMC allocation for cane-based); El Nino impact on Bioseed (cotton inventory overhang); Geopolitical supply chain disruptions.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; emphasizes resilience, balance sheet strength, and policy advocacy (MIP/Add for PVC); transparent about margin headwinds in Sugar and volatility in Vinyls.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: ECH plant selling 70-75% output externally rather than captive consumption due to smaller LER capacity; Fertilizer subsidy outstanding increased to INR 189 Cr; PVC import duty waiver ends June 2026, creating binary outcome for H2 pricing.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Our balance sheet remains strong, giving us resilience from external volatility and enabling us to pursue growth", alongside a stated focus on "disciplined capital allocation".
- Net Debt of Rs 1,649 cr in Q1'27 vs Rs 1,481 cr in Q1'26; ROCE of 13.6% vs 13.2%, computed by the deck on the average of capital employed at the end of the last five quarters and trailing 12 month PBIT, with capital employed excluding CWIP and liquid investments.
- Capital employed includes CWIP of Rs 411 crs at 30th June 2026 vs Rs 806 crs at 30th June 2025, indicating the project pipeline moving into commissioning.
- Inorganic deployment: acquisition of 53% stake in DNV Global Pvt Ltd (Hardware) in May 2025 and 100% stake in HSCL (advanced materials, viz. Epoxy) in August 2025, plus the proposed salt works acquisition under regulatory approval.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Only company in the country which manufactures PVC Resin through the Calcium Carbide route as against the alternate Ethylene route
- Oldest manufacturer of PVC Resins currently operational in the country, with a rich experience of six decades in the business
- Second largest caustic player in the country, with Bharuch being the largest single location caustic manufacturing plant
- Highly integrated and energy-intensive chemicals and vinyl operations supported by 345 MW captive power with flexi fuel option plus captive renewable power, reducing energy cost sensitivity
- Internal integration of chlorine, calcium carbide and PVC resin - carbide is captively consumed for PVC, and PVC resin is captively used for Fenesta's uPVC window and door profiles
- Swing capability in the Vinyl business to sell more PVC Resin or Calcium Carbide depending upon the margins of these products
- Diversified business model across chemicals, sugar and ethanol, agri-inputs and building systems, which management credits for resilient performance
- Financial prudence with a strong balance sheet and disciplined working capital management supporting continuity amid commodity volatility
- Consumer-facing brands - Fenesta Building Systems and Shriram Farm Solutions - alongside the commodity chemicals base
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Climate change and carbon regulation exposure — Material because of the Company's energy-intensive manufacturing operations, evolving carbon regulations and climate variability affecting agricultural value chains, creating risks of input cost volatility, regulatory compliance and disruption in feedstock availability. Management flags that frequent regulatory requirements setting GEI targets for energy-intensive sectors may pose a challenge to compliance and have a negative financial implication, while the low-carbon transition is also an opportunity through energy efficiency, renewable adoption and green products such as bio-based chemicals and ethanol.
- Sustainable supply chain and input availability disruption — The Company depends on raw material availability, farmer networks and logistics efficiency amid rising ESG expectations across value chains; disruption or non-compliance creates cost, quality and reputational risk. Management explicitly states supply chain disruptions due to geo-political or other unforeseen circumstances may impact it negatively financially. Mitigation runs through responsible sourcing, supplier codes of conduct, contractual obligations and periodic supplier performance monitoring, plus collaboration with key suppliers and farmer networks for input security.
- Health and safety in hazardous chemical operations — Material given operations involving hazardous processes, chemicals and a contractor workforce; gaps in safety management can affect employees, contractors, communities and business continuity and create regulatory and operational risk. Managed via an integrated management system aligned with ISO 45001, contractor safety requirements, emergency preparedness, audits and tracking of leading and lagging indicators including near misses and incident rates.
- Waste management and environmental liability — Material due to regulatory obligations on handling and disposal of industrial waste, potential environmental liabilities and rising expectations on resource circularity; inefficient practices create compliance, cost and reputational risk. Mitigated through a structured waste framework covering segregation, handling, treatment and disposal, resource recovery from by-products such as fly ash and sludge, and tracking of waste metrics at operational and corporate levels.
- Talent attraction, retention and succession readiness — Business performance and long-term growth depend on attracting, developing and retaining skilled talent; weak engagement or capability gaps create risks around attrition, productivity and succession readiness. Addressed through structured leadership and capability programmes, engagement processes, training calendars and inclusion initiatives such as ALDP, stakeholder management workshops, 'SheLeads' and 'Campus to Corporate Learning'.
- Community relations and social licence to operate — Material due to dependence on local communities, particularly in agri-linked regions, for stable operations and long-term growth; inadequate engagement can result in social risk, operational disruption and reduced stakeholder trust. Managed through structured stakeholder engagement, CSR governance, impact assessment and targeted interventions in livelihoods, healthcare, education and agriculture.
- Human rights and labour practices across contract labour and extended value chains — Material due to regulatory requirements, stakeholder expectations and reliance on contract labour and extended value chains, where non-compliance can lead to legal, reputational and operational risk. Managed through policies, codes of conduct and compliance mechanisms enforcing fair labour practices, non-discrimination and safe working conditions including for the contract workforce, with supplier and contractor compliance addressed through contractual requirements and grievance redressal mechanisms.

business.body:
- FY 2025-26 revenue split stated as Agri Rural 56% (Sugar & Ethanol, Shriram Farm Solutions, Bioseed, Fertilizer), Chemicals & Vinyl 34% and Building Material Products 8% (Fenesta Building Systems).
- Chemicals & Vinyl described as "highly integrated operations with multiple revenue streams", with chemicals at Bharuch (Gujarat) and Kota (Rajasthan) and Vinyl at Kota only.

business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [PVC regulation] "Custom duty waivers led to continued Chinese imports in India. Since July 16, the custom duty has been reinstated and on July 24, 'Minimum import price' on low priced suspension grade PVC has been introduced for 6 months and can be extended" - expected to aid domestic prices.
- [Ethanol policy] Blending reached 20.00% in ESY 25-26 (as on 30/06/2026) vs 19.20% in ESY 24-25; management states the ethanol blending ecosystem "still requires decisive and sustained government policy interventions regarding feedstock pricing and alternate usage mandates".
- [Exceptional/tax] Q1 FY27 PAT includes Rs 474.3 cr tax adjustment on a favourable judgement under Section 80-IA of the Income Tax Act, 1961 for previous years, and one-time exceptional items of Rs 79.4 cr from profit on sale of land and stake sale to form a JV; the deck states "Effective normal PAT is Rs 147 cr".
- [Fertilizer subsidy] Subsidy outstanding as at 30th June 2026 is Rs 292 cr (LY Rs 236 cr) vs Rs 189 cr as on 31st March 2026.
- [Sugar cycle] Global sugar supply & demand for SS 2026-27 expected to be in deficit of 0.7 MMT (vs 2.5 MMT surplus LY) mainly due to lower production in Thailand & Europe by 3.9 MMT; SS 2025-26 in India expected to have ended with a stock of 3.8 MMT (LY 5.1 MMT).
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company operates a chemicals and vinyl business that makes caustic soda, chlorine, hydrogen, hydrogen peroxide, hydrochloric acid, aluminium chloride, stable bleaching powder, sodium hypochlorite and advanced materials (glycerine, epichlorohydrin and epoxy resins), together with PVC resins, calcium carbide and polymer compounds, all supported by captive power and internal integration of chlorine and calcium carbide. Alongside this it runs a sugar and ethanol business, agri-input businesses (Shriram Farm Solutions, Bioseed and Fertilizer) and Fenesta Building Systems, which converts captively produced PVC resin into uPVC window and door profiles. Its customers span industrial chemical users, PVC fabricators and pipe makers, farmers and rural consumers, and retail/consumer buyers of windows and doors.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Invest to increase scale, drive cost efficiencies and diversify revenue streams in the chemicals business, consistently matching capacity augmentation with downstream integration, greener and more efficient sources of energy and operational excellence
- Scale the advanced materials business (including the recently acquired Hindusthan Specialty Chemical Limited) and explore the next wave of growth for chemicals
- Reinforce the digital framework of the chemicals business to improve operational efficiency
- Accelerate downstream integration into Aluminium Chloride, Calcium Chloride and ECH, plus captive renewable power projects, to improve margin capture and reduce feedstock and energy cost sensitivity
- Use the Vinyl business's swing capability to sell more PVC Resin or Calcium Carbide depending on relative product margins, and maximise margins through cost reduction initiatives, capex and evaluation of new models that enhance process efficiency
- Strengthen the polymer compounding position through the newly formed joint venture with Teknor Apex, which also allows Teknor Apex to expand its footprint in Asia
- Add renewable hybrid power at both complexes (board-approved 48 MW at Bharuch augmenting the existing 50 MW, and 68 MW for Kota) to reduce cost and advance sustainability initiatives
- In sugar, having built fully integrated complexes capable of capturing full downstream value across all four sugar factories, focus on improving sugarcane productivity and quality through dedicated cane development so farmers get higher yields and mills get better recoveries and volumes
- Diversify the sugar product mix (CBG, potash), strengthen farmer engagement programmes to improve cane quality, and pursue merchant ethanol and power sales to optimise realisations
- In Fenesta, set up newer revenue platforms and enhance capacities, innovate new products across verticals, and grow both geographically and by increasing product offerings in Windows, Doors, Facades and Hardware
- Evolve Fenesta's positioning as a comprehensive 'lifestyle partner', expanding its footprint in the building materials category to capture a larger share of the consumer wallet
- In Shriram Farm Solutions, empower farmers through science-driven, trusted and differentiated agri-input solutions across seeds and crop inputs
- The Company's stated approach is reinvestment-led: surplus funds were utilised for project capex, which is the reason given for the increase in net debt during the year, while gearing was described as remaining low. Growth capital is directed at scale, integration and cost efficiency - capacity expansion matched with downstream integration, greener and more efficient energy sourcing through group-captive renewable SPVs, and bolt-on acquisitions for backward integration (windows and doors hardware, and the Board-approved salt mines) and forward integration (advanced materials). The Company also recycles capital out of non-core control positions, having sold a 50% stake in Shriram Polytech Ltd. to form a joint venture with Teknor Apex B.V. Governance of this spending runs through the Board and Audit Committee, with the Directors affirming adequate and effective internal financial controls, cost records maintained under Section 148(1), and unmodified statutory and secretarial audit reports.
- Climate action is being advanced through renewable energy sourcing, biomass and bioenergy initiatives, decarbonisation projects and climate-responsive planning for vulnerable agri and seed value chains
- A portfolio of decarbonisation actions including wind-solar hybrid sourcing, higher biomass and bagasse-based energy use, process efficiency upgrades and improved equipment performance
- Regular MIS-based review of energy and GHG indicators at both site and corporate level, with climate risk assessment being strengthened through structured climate risk and scenario-based review
- Green product offerings such as bio-based chemicals and ethanol identified as a transition opportunity, alongside improved access to ESG-aligned capital and markets
- Circularity and resource recovery, including utilisation of by-products such as fly ash and sludge to reduce environmental liabilities and dependence on virgin raw materials, with waste generation and disposal metrics tracked and reviewed
- Health and safety managed through an integrated management system aligned with ISO 45001, embedded across operations, tracking both leading and lagging indicators including near misses and incident rates
- Diversity and capability building through ALDP, stakeholder management workshops, 'SheLeads' and 'Campus to Corporate Learning' programmes
- CSR and community development interventions in livelihoods, healthcare, education and agriculture, with impact assessment, feedback and consultation processes and periodic review of programme outcomes
- Responsible sourcing across the value chain via supplier codes of conduct, contractual ESG obligations and periodic monitoring of supplier performance, quality and compliance for traceability and input security
- A Whistle Blower Policy administered by a designated Ombudsperson, extended to employees (full-time, part-time and contractual), suppliers, contractors, vendors, business associates and customers, permitting anonymous reporting without fear of retaliation, with serious misconduct reported to the Audit Committee
- Stakeholder grievance redressal platforms for each stakeholder group, including dedicated customer care platforms for the Sugar, SFS, Bioseed and Fenesta businesses

outlook.body: In line with a strategy to strengthen businesses through scale, integration and cost efficiency, DCM Shriram is executing a range of growth projects. At Bharuch, an Aluminium Chloride expansion of 100 TPD together with a 225 TPD Calcium Chloride facility is planned for commissioning by Q1 FY27, and the Anhydrous Sodium Sulphate (AnSS) project is expected to be completed by Q1 FY27; both chlorine-downstream projects are described as being in advanced stages of commissioning. An energy saving project at Bharuch is expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY28, and renewable solar-plus-wind power at Bharuch is being enhanced by a further 48 MW (peak) via the SPV group-captive route, augmenting the existing 50 MW hybrid capacity. In advanced materials, a 36 KTPA Formulated Resins capacity expansion is planned in Hindusthan Speciality Chemicals Limited by Q2 FY28. For Fenesta, an aluminium extrusion plant at Kota is expected to be commissioned by Q2 FY27. At the Kota complex, 68 MW peak (average about 34 MW) of renewable solar-plus-wind power via the SPV group-captive route is due by Q1 FY27, with injection of 15 MW (average) already started from 4th May 2026. Beyond these, the Board approved entering into a definitive agreement towards the acquisition of salt mines to facilitate backward integration of the chemicals business into salt, subject to customary regulatory approvals. During FY26 the Company commissioned projects at a cumulative investment of about Rs. 1106 crore: a 52000 TPA Epichlorohydrin facility with glycerine purification (partially in Oct'25 and the remainder in Apr'26), a 6.6 MW enhancement in renewable solar-plus-wind power for Bharuch via the SPV group-captive route, acquisition of a 53% equity stake in DNV Global Pvt. Ltd. for backward integration into windows and doors hardware, and acquisition of a 100% equity stake in Hindusthan Speciality Chemicals Ltd. for forward integration into advanced materials. After the year end the Company sold a 50% stake in its subsidiary Shriram Polytech Ltd. to Teknor Apex B.V. to form a joint venture combining Shriram Polytech's Indian vinyl compounds manufacturing base with Teknor Apex's global expertise in specialized formulations. Management states that the chemicals business has consistently matched capacity augmentation with downstream integration, greener and more efficient energy sources and operational excellence, and believes these steps will significantly strengthen its businesses.

outlook.body:
- Domestic caustic soda demand has grown at ~5% CAGR over the last 10 years and is expected to grow in the same range with growth in consuming sectors (alumina, textile, pulp & paper, soap & detergents, pharmaceuticals) and in downstream chlorine industries
- The Indian caustic industry has ~6.4 million MTPA installed capacity (~5.9% of global) with the top 4 players - Grasim, DCM Shriram, GACL and Epigral - accounting for ~54% of it
- Advanced materials continues to witness healthy growth led by Epoxy, with all key players adding capacity on rising domestic demand, supported by Anti-Dumping Duty levied by the Government on both ECH and Epoxy
- Hydrogen peroxide remains oversupplied in the domestic market with Bangladesh dumping material into India on the back of subsidised natural gas prices there
- PVC demand, an infrastructure-linked polymer, is expected to grow ~6-7% in line with India's GDP, supported by government-led infrastructure and housing initiatives, the Jal Jeevan Mission, smart cities and higher farm income; FY26 domestic PVC demand is estimated at ~4.5 million tonnes against installed capacity of ~1.5 million TPA
- Pipes and fittings account for ~80% of India's PVC consumption versus ~46% globally, tying demand to construction and agriculture
- India is the top import destination for PVC globally and continues to absorb surplus global supply; China, South Korea, Japan and Taiwan account for 80% of PVC imports into India, and the domestic demand-supply gap will persist and be met by imports
- Calcium carbide demand is expected to remain stable in FY27, supported by continued infrastructure spending and sustained requirements from dissolved acetylene gas and de-sulphurizing compounds in the expanding steel sector
- Vinyl realizations were pressured as international carbide prices fell from an average $686/MT for PE Mar'25 to $637/MT for PE Mar'26 and PVC from $814/MT to $721/MT over the same periods
- The Indian PVC compounds market is expanding, with estimated total demand of ~3.6 lakh MT per year in 2025-26 and ~5% import share
- World sugar balance is expected to be in surplus of ~2.9 MMT in SS 25-26; India is structurally a sugar surplus nation with current season production expected at ~28.3 MMT after ~3.1 MMT diversion to ethanol against consumption close to 28.1 MMT, exports allowed of 2 MMT likely closing at 1 MMT, and a closing stock of ~4.3 MMT
- On ethanol, OMCs allocated 1058 crore litres in ESY 25-26 against an industry offer of 1776 crore litres (60% allocation), with grain and sugar-based feedstock at 72% and 28% respectively; countrywide distillery capacity is outstripping demand and ethanol disposal is emerging as a major industry challenge requiring proactive policy support
- Sugar and ethanol economics are sensitive to policy changes (allocation, export permissions, blending mandates) and to seasonal cane yields
- CBG and potash businesses added in FY26 are expected to provide incremental margin stability by monetising by-products and reducing dependence on sugar-only realisations
- Indian agriculture is in a structural transition; despite uneven monsoons, commodity price volatility and geopolitical disruption, the medium-to-long term outlook remains resilient on rising food demand, focus on farm productivity, a shift to high-value crops and sustainability-led practices, with farmers increasingly value-conscious and prioritising reliable, yield-enhancing solutions

risks.note: Material because of the Company's energy-intensive manufacturing operations, evolving carbon regulations and climate variability affecting agricultural value chains, creating risks of input cost volatility, regulatory compliance and disruption in feedstock availability. Management flags that frequent regulatory requirements setting GEI targets for energy-intensive sectors may pose a challenge to compliance and have a negative financial implication, while the low-carbon transition is also an opportunity through energy efficiency, renewable adoption and green products such as bio-based chemicals and ethanol.
risks.risk: Climate change and carbon regulation exposure

risks.note: The Company depends on raw material availability, farmer networks and logistics efficiency amid rising ESG expectations across value chains; disruption or non-compliance creates cost, quality and reputational risk. Management explicitly states supply chain disruptions due to geo-political or other unforeseen circumstances may impact it negatively financially. Mitigation runs through responsible sourcing, supplier codes of conduct, contractual obligations and periodic supplier performance monitoring, plus collaboration with key suppliers and farmer networks for input security.
risks.risk: Sustainable supply chain and input availability disruption

risks.note: Material given operations involving hazardous processes, chemicals and a contractor workforce; gaps in safety management can affect employees, contractors, communities and business continuity and create regulatory and operational risk. Managed via an integrated management system aligned with ISO 45001, contractor safety requirements, emergency preparedness, audits and tracking of leading and lagging indicators including near misses and incident rates.
risks.risk: Health and safety in hazardous chemical operations

risks.note: Material due to regulatory obligations on handling and disposal of industrial waste, potential environmental liabilities and rising expectations on resource circularity; inefficient practices create compliance, cost and reputational risk. Mitigated through a structured waste framework covering segregation, handling, treatment and disposal, resource recovery from by-products such as fly ash and sludge, and tracking of waste metrics at operational and corporate levels.

Business performance and long-term growth depend on attracting, developing and retaining skilled talent; weak engagement or capability gaps create risks around attrition, productivity and succession readiness. Addressed through structured leadership and capability programmes, engagement processes, training calendars and inclusion initiatives such as ALDP, stakeholder management workshops, 'SheLeads' and 'Campus to Corporate Learning'.
risks.risk: Talent attraction, retention and succession readiness

risks.note: Material due to dependence on local communities, particularly in agri-linked regions, for stable operations and long-term growth; inadequate engagement can result in social risk, operational disruption and reduced stakeholder trust. Managed through structured stakeholder engagement, CSR governance, impact assessment and targeted interventions in livelihoods, healthcare, education and agriculture.
risks.risk: Community relations and social licence to operate

risks.note: Material due to regulatory requirements, stakeholder expectations and reliance on contract labour and extended value chains, where non-compliance can lead to legal, reputational and operational risk. Managed through policies, codes of conduct and compliance mechanisms enforcing fair labour practices, non-discrimination and safe working conditions including for the contract workforce, with supplier and contractor compliance addressed through contractual requirements and grievance redressal mechanisms.
risks.risk: Human rights and labour practices across contract labour and extended value chains
